dedupe_keys.name: nauru sustainable and climate resilient connectivity project aiwo port

description: This Asian Development Bank project, formerly the Nauru Port Development Project, rebuilds the only port of Nauru at Aiwo to be efficient, reliable and resilient to climate change. It builds a wharf, breakwater and berth pocket, reconstructs port buildings and the container storage area, and strengthens the Nauru Maritime and Port Authority, with grants of about 3 million dollars for design, 21.3 million and 15 million from the Asian Development Fund, 14.1 million from Australia and 26.9 million from the Green Climate Fund. The page reports that the new wharf became operational on 3 September 2022, the liquid bulk fuel pipeline on 12 September 2023 and a reverse osmosis plant was handed to the utility, while the northern container yard, internal road, dredging and buildings were awaited; slow production of aggregate and armour rock is the main constraint, and a revolving maintenance fund was set up. It also documents safeguard issues such as vibration affecting dilapidated homes next to the site. Coverage: one port on a small Pacific island. Access: free ADB project page with linked documents. Licence and cost: free to read, ADB terms. Caveats: a progress record, not an evaluation; design standards and climate criteria are in linked documents, not summarised here. It supports climate adaptation and resilience planning for small island ports, and relates to the Nauru census household data in the catalogue.
